q: How does gastroschisis differ from exomphalos?
o: Gastroschisis is not covered by peritoneum; exomphalos is and has more associated anomalies
why: Exomphalos is associated with other congenital abnormalities.

q: How is the exposed bowel protected before surgery?
o: Covered with cling film to reduce heat and fluid loss
why: Also NG decompression and fluid resuscitation.

q: What causes raised airway pressures during closure?
o: Raised intra-abdominal pressure from a tight closure
why: Use a staged closure (silo) if pressures are high.

q: What surgical complication follows a too-tight closure?
why: Bowel ischaemia, renal impairment and ventilation problems.

q: What is the usual destination after closure?
why: An epidural may allow earlier extubation.
